content.title: Welcome AKU - SONAM Class of 2021
content.summary: AKU SONAM receives new undergraduate class

content.text: Monday January 28 2019 saw SONAM Kenya welcome a fresh crop of nurses and midwives to its Bachelor of Science in Nursing and Midwifery classes. The new students were on campus for a three-day orientation before the semester officially begins this February. The orientation is designed to help the students get acquainted with the school and how it functions in order to prepare them for the beginning of classes.

Professor Sharon Brownie, Dean of AKU-SONAM, welcomed the class and thereafter members of faculty were on hand to deliver the orientation. Acting Academic Head, Ms Isabel Kambo, and BScN Course Coordinator, Ms Gladys Mbuthia, had the newest class on campus engage in an interesting exercise.

Ms Mbuthia and Ms Kambo asked the class to share their reasons for, and expectations once, joining AKU-SONAM.  When I reviewed the material, it was evident that most frontline healthcare professionals choose to study with AKU-SONAM because they believe that they will receive quality education, which is at par with international standards. The incoming class comprised of both BScN and BScM students, also believe that enrolling at AKU will enable them to improve their skills and position them as leaders in the next generation of healthcare workers in the region. They are interested in acquiring the knowledge and skills to better serve the communities they come from.

They also had a session with the University Associate Registrar, Mr Stanley Awuonda, who took them through what the Registrar's office does while explaining the Student Handbook to them. They were thereafter, taken on a tour of the campus by the Programmes Assistant, Ms Rose Mutwiwa.
Ms Mbuthia and Ms Kambo asked the class to share their reasons for, and expectations once, joining AKU-SONAM.
